US consumer confidence is collapsing.

The Consumer Confidence Index dropped -6.7 points in September, to 81.9, its lowest since April 2014.

This marks its 4th consecutive monthly decline, totaling -11.2 points.

The Present Situation Index fell -7.9 points, to 109.3, its lowest since February 2021.

At the same time, the Expectations Index fell -5.9 points, to 63.6, its lowest since April 2025, marking its 3rd consecutive monthly decline.

Over the last 6 months, confidence across all age groups and nearly all income groups has declined.

Consumers are also increasingly citing high prices, the cost of goods and services, and oil and gasoline prices as major factors weighing on the economy.

US consumer confidence is at crisis levels.

BREAKING: Flavio Bolsonaro has defeated Brazilian President Lula da Silva in the first round of Brazil’s presidential election.

Bolsonaro received 47.3% of the vote, compared to 44.8% for Lula, with 98% of votes counted.

Neither candidate reached the 50% threshold needed to win outright, sending the election to an October 25th runoff.

This marks marking Lula’s first presidential election defeat since 1998.

The US stock market is in its own league.

US stock market cap now accounts for 45% of the world equity market value, the most among any other major country or region.

This is nearly triple the combined proportion of China and Hong Kong, at 16%.

Europe and the rest of Asia-Pacific follow, accounting for 13% and 11% of global market cap, respectively.

By comparison, Japan, the world's 3rd-largest stock market, represents just 6%.

Meanwhile, the Middle East and Africa account for 5%, while Canada and Latin America make up 3% and 1%, respectively.

The scale of the US equity market relative to the rest of the world is unprecedented.

US layoff announcements are declining:

US job cut announcements dropped -20% YoY in September, to 43,281, the lowest September total since 2022.

In Q3, planned layoffs fell -36% YoY, to 129,591, the lowest quarterly figure since Q4 2023.

This brings year-to-date announcements down -39% YoY, to 573,195, the lowest since 2022.

This is also the 7th month of 2026 with job cuts below the corresponding month of the prior year.

The tech sector saw the most announcements last month and year-to-date, at 10,799 and 165,925 respectively.

Meanwhile, market and economic conditions accounted for 8,789 announced job cuts in September, or 20% of all layoffs, bringing the year-to-date total to 114,124, the 2nd-highest of any cited reason after AI.

US employers are taking a wait-and-see approach to layoffs.
